category: PCB Editor libraries, manufacturing output, documentation & scripting
description: Turning a routed OrCAD PCB Editor board into a manufacturable, documented release and automating the process: padstack and footprint authoring, reports, Gerber/NC drill/ODB++/IPC-2581/assembly/3D outputs, back annotation, recorded .scr scripts, the SKILL (axl*) programming API and the standalone Cadence command-line utilities.

tools.name: Symbol / Footprint Editor (.dra / .psm)
tools.description: Creates package symbols. A footprint is authored in a drawing file (.dra) containing pins built from padstacks, the assembly and silkscreen outlines, the place-bound (courtyard) shape, the pin-1 marker and the refdes text; saving compiles it to a .psm that the board loads. The same editor produces mechanical, format and shape symbols.
tools.usage: File > New > drawing type 'Package symbol'; Layout > Pins to add pins; File > Create Symbol to compile the .psm

parameters.name: Package Symbol
parameters.description: Standard footprint with pins, outlines and a place-bound.

parameters.name: Mechanical Symbol
parameters.description: Non-electrical item such as a mounting bracket or keep-out region.

parameters.name: Format Symbol
parameters.description: Drawing border/title block.

parameters.name: Shape Symbol
parameters.description: Reusable copper shape such as a thermal pad pattern.

tools.example: File > New > Package symbol 'SOIC8'; Layout > Pins > padstack SMD_60x22, 8 pins, 50 mil pitch; draw the Package Geometry/Assembly_Top outline and the Place_Bound_Top; File > Create Symbol.
tools.notes: A footprint without a Place_Bound_Top shape has no courtyard, so component-to-component spacing DRC cannot work.

tools.name: Padstack Editor
tools.description: Creates and edits padstacks — the per-layer pad, thermal relief, anti-pad, soldermask and pastemask geometry plus the drill definition. Padstack type covers through, blind/buried, microvia, SMD and mechanical/slot holes; the drill tab sets the hole size, plating, tolerance, drill symbol and whether the hole is a slot. Correct thermal relief definitions here are what makes plane connections solderable.
tools.usage: Standalone Padstack Editor application, or Tools > Padstack > Modify Design Padstack…

parameters.name: Drill hole
parameters.description: Diameter, plated/non-plated, tolerance, slot geometry.

parameters.name: Regular Pad / Thermal Relief / Anti Pad
parameters.description: Per-layer (Begin/Default Internal/End) geometry for signal, plane-connected and plane-clearance cases.

parameters.name: Soldermask / Pastemask
parameters.description: Mask openings, usually a fixed expansion over the copper pad.

parameters.name: Padstack usage
parameters.description: Through, Blind/Buried, Microvia, SMD Pin, Bond Finger, Mechanical hole.

tools.example: Padstack Editor > New > Via > drill 0.3 mm plated, regular pad 0.6 mm all layers, anti-pad 0.9 mm, thermal relief 4 spokes 0.2 mm > save VIA_03_06.pad.

tools.name: Auto Silkscreen
tools.description: Repositions reference designator text so that it does not sit on pads, vias, holes or other silkscreen, obeying minimum line width and keep-out rules. It converts an unreadable mass of overlapping refdes into an assembly-ready silkscreen in one pass, with manual touch-up afterwards for the few it cannot solve.
tools.usage: Manufacture > Silkscreen… (Auto Silkscreen)
tools.example: Manufacture > Silkscreen > scope: whole design, min line width 5 mil, allow rotation > Silkscreen; then fix the handful of parts it reports as unresolvable.

tools.name: Dimensioning
tools.description: Adds fabrication and assembly dimensions to the drawing: linear, datum, chamfer, radial and angular dimensions plus balloons and leader lines, drawn on a documentation subclass. Dimension parameters (units, precision, arrow style, text block, tolerance display) are set once and reused.
tools.usage: Manufacture > Dimension/Draft > Linear dimension | Datum dimension | Radial | Angular | Balloon | Leader line; Parameters for the style
tools.example: Manufacture > Dimension/Draft > Parameters > units mm, 2 decimals; then Linear dimension across the board outline and to each mounting hole.

tools.name: Reports
tools.description: Generates text reports from the board database: Bill of Materials, Net List, Component (placement), Unplaced Components, Unconnected Pins, Net Delay/Length, Drill, Testprep, Etch Length by Layer and many more. Reports can be previewed, written to file and re-run after changes, making them the manual counterpart to extracta for extracting data.
tools.usage: Tools > Reports… > select one or more report types > Report
tools.example: Tools > Reports > tick 'Bill of Material Report' and 'Unconnected Pins Report' > Report > save both to the project folder.

tools.name: Artwork (Gerber output)
tools.description: Generates the photoplot files. Each artwork film is a named set of layer/subclass combinations (e.g. TOP = ETCH/TOP + PIN/TOP + VIA CLASS/TOP); the Device Type selects the format — Gerber RS-274X (extended, with embedded apertures) is the normal choice, with Gerber 4x00/6x00 legacy formats and Gerber X2 where supported. Film options set undefined line width, shape bounding box, mirroring and drawing offsets.
tools.usage: Manufacture > Artwork… > General Parameters tab (device type, format, units, suppress leading zeros) > Film Control tab (films and their subclasses) > Create Artwork

parameters.name: Device type
parameters.description: Gerber RS-274X, Gerber 4x00/6x00, Barco DPF, MDA.

parameters.name: Format
parameters.description: Integer and decimal digit counts, e.g. 2.5 for mils or 4.4 for millimetres.

parameters.name: Undefined line width
parameters.description: Width used for zero-width geometry; leaving it at 0 produces missing lines in the output.

parameters.name: Film options
parameters.description: Per-film mirror, negative/positive, offset and rotation.

tools.example: Manufacture > Artwork > device RS-274X, format 2.5, suppress leading zeroes > select all films > Create Artwork; then view the output with the Gerber viewer before release.
tools.notes: Always re-check that every plane layer's film is set to negative if the cross-section says negative, and that shapes are Smooth-updated before plotting.

tools.name: NC Drill output
tools.description: Produces the Excellon drill files and associated tool table. NC Parameters sets format, units, leading/trailing zero suppression and whether separate files are written per drill span; NC Drill runs the generation; Drill Legend places the symbol legend table on the drawing and Drill Customization edits the symbol assigned to each tool.
tools.usage: Manufacture > NC > NC Parameters…, NC Drill…, Drill Legend…, Drill Customization…

parameters.name: Separate files for plated/non-plated
parameters.description: Splits PTH and NPTH into different programs, which most fabricators expect.

parameters.name: Repeat codes / Enhanced Excellon
parameters.description: Output dialect options.

parameters.name: Drill legend
parameters.description: Table of drill symbol, size, plating and quantity placed on the fabrication drawing.

tools.example: Manufacture > NC > NC Parameters (format 2.5, trailing zero suppression, separate plated/non-plated) > NC Drill > Drill; then Drill Legend to place the table.

tools.name: IPC-2581 and ODB++ export
tools.description: Intelligent, single-file manufacturing handoff formats that carry stackup, netlist, drill, copper, mask, paste, component placement and DFM data together, removing the ambiguity of a folder of Gerbers. IPC-2581 (Revision B/C) is the open standard; ODB++ is the widely supported Valor format. Both are preferred over Gerber when the fabricator accepts them.
tools.usage: File > Export > IPC2581…; File > Export > ODB++ (Manufacture menu in some builds)
tools.example: File > Export > IPC2581 > Revision C > include netlist and component data > export board.xml; confirm it opens in the fabricator's viewer.
tools.notes: Still generate a drawing PDF alongside: notes, finishes and tolerances that live in drawing text are not fully carried by either format.

tools.name: Assembly and pick-and-place output
tools.description: Assembly deliverables: the component placement report gives every part's refdes, X/Y centroid, rotation and side for the pick-and-place machine, while the assembly drawing films (Assembly_Top/Bottom subclasses plus refdes and outlines) are plotted as artwork or exported to PDF. Together with the BOM they are the complete assembly package.
tools.usage: Tools > Reports > Component Report / Placement Report; Manufacture > Artwork with an assembly film; File > Export > PDF
tools.example: Tools > Reports > 'Component Report' > save placement.rpt; Manufacture > Artwork > film ASSY_TOP > Create Artwork.
tools.notes: Confirm the rotation convention the assembler expects — Allegro reports the symbol's rotation, which may differ from the machine's zero-degree reference.

tools.name: 3D Canvas and STEP export
tools.description: Renders the board and its components in 3D for mechanical checking, with cross-sectioning, measurement and interference detection between component bodies and the enclosure. STEP models attached to footprints are used for the solids, and the whole assembly can be exported as a STEP file for the mechanical CAD team.
tools.usage: View > 3D Canvas; File > Export > STEP…; attach models with the STEP mapping file / Setup > Step Package Mapping
tools.example: View > 3D Canvas > enable the cutting plane on the X axis to inspect connector clearance; File > Export > STEP > board.step for the MCAD handoff.
tools.notes: Components without a mapped STEP model appear as simple extrusions of their place-bound, which is enough for height checks but not for connector mating.

tools.name: Back annotation / feedback to Capture
tools.description: Sends layout-side changes — renumbered reference designators, gate and pin swaps performed for routability — back to the schematic. PCB Editor writes a swap/feedback file which Capture's Tools > Back Annotate consumes. In the OrCAD X flow this is superseded by Design Sync, which reconciles both directions interactively.
tools.usage: File > Export > Logic (feedback) — then in Capture: Tools > Back Annotate; or PCB > Design Sync in OrCAD X
tools.example: After swapping two NAND gates for routability: File > Export > Logic > feedback file; in Capture Tools > Back Annotate > PCB Editor > select the file.

tools.name: Script record and replay (.scr)
tools.description: PCB Editor's zero-programming automation. File > Script names a script, Record captures every subsequent command into an ASCII .scr file, and Stop ends the recording. The script is replayed from the same dialog or from the board command line with `replay`. Adding `scriptmode +invisible` as the first line suppresses the dialogs during playback so it runs silently.
tools.usage: File > Script… > name + Record / Stop; replay with File > Script > Browse + Replay, or `replay <file>.scr` in the command window

parameters.name: Record / Stop
parameters.description: Start and end capture of commands into the script.

parameters.name: scriptmode +invisible
parameters.description: First line of the .scr; runs the script without opening its dialogs.

tools.example:
# record: File > Script > 'grid_5' > Record > Setup > Grids > set 5/5 > Stop
# replay from the command window:
replay ./grid_5.scr
tools.notes: Scripts are plain text and can be hand-edited, which is often easier than re-recording.

tools.name: alias (command shortcuts)
tools.description: Binds a name or a function key to a command string in the PCB Editor command window, including replaying a script. Aliases defined in the session last until it ends; putting them in the env file under the user's pcbenv directory makes them permanent, which is how teams standardise shortcut keys across a group.
tools.usage: alias <name-or-key> <command string>
tools.example:
alias grid5 replay ./grid_5.scr
alias F5 "zoom fit"
# then type grid5 in the command window, or press F5
tools.notes: `funckey` binds a single character to a command in the same way; both are commonly collected in the user's `env` file.

tools.name: SKILL: axlDBGetDesign and the design object
tools.description: The root of the PCB Editor SKILL API. `axlDBGetDesign()` returns the DBID of the open board, whose attributes are reached with the `->` operator: `design->components`, `->nets`, `->layers`, `->name`, `->units`. Each component in turn exposes `->refdes`, `->xy`, `->rotation`, `->isMirrored`, `->pins` and so on, so a handful of lines produces a full placement report.
tools.usage:
design = axlDBGetDesign()
foreach( obj design->components … )
tools.example:
procedure( comp_loc()
  let( (design)
    design = axlDBGetDesign()
    foreach( comp design->components
      printf("%s %L\n" comp->refdes comp->xy))))
comp_loc()
tools.notes: Use the `?` inspection operator in the command window to list an object's available attributes when the reference manual is not to hand.

tools.name: SKILL: selection and find filter
tools.description: SKILL selects objects through the same mechanism as interactive commands: `axlSetFindFilter` programmatically enables or disables the Find Filter classes, then a selection function such as `axlSingleSelectBox`, `axlSingleSelectPoint` or `axlSelectByName` builds the selection set, which `axlGetSelSet` returns for processing. Subset/add variants extend or reduce the set, mirroring the interactive model.
tools.usage:
axlSetFindFilter(?enabled list("noall" "clines") ?onButtons list("clines"))
axlSingleSelectBox(nil)
sel = axlGetSelSet()
tools.example:
axlSetFindFilter(?enabled '("noall" "clines") ?onButtons '("clines"))
axlSingleSelectBox(nil)
foreach( seg axlGetSelSet() printf("%L\n" seg->length))
tools.notes: `axlSingleSelectBox` clears the existing selection set first; use the add-variants to accumulate.

tools.name: SKILL: user interface functions
tools.description: Blocking UI calls that let a script ask the user something mid-run: `axlUIPrompt` for a typed value, `axlUIYesNo` for a confirmer, `axlUIConfirm` for a message, plus a file browser and multiple-choice dialog. For richer input, `axlFormCreate` builds a real PCB Editor form from a .form file and `axlFormGetField` / `axlFormSetField` read and write its fields, with a callback procedure invoked on OK and on field changes.
tools.usage:
axlUIPrompt("prompt" "default")
axlUIYesNo("question")
axlFormCreate(formName formFile nil callbackProc t)
axlFormGetField(form "fieldName")
tools.example:
ratio = axlUIPrompt("Aspect ratio:" "0.5")
when( axlUIYesNo("Add DRC markers for the results?")
  addDrcs = t)
tools.notes: These calls block until the user responds, so they cannot be used in a truly unattended batch run.

tools.name: SKILL: creating objects and DRC markers
tools.description: The `axlDBCreate*` family writes into the board database: lines and paths, shapes, text, vias and pins, plus `axlDBCreateExternalDRC` which drops a custom DRC marker at a location with a message. Custom checks (aspect ratio of connect-line segments, silkscreen conflicts, company-specific DFM) are therefore reported through the normal DRC browser instead of a separate log.
tools.usage:
axlDBCreateExternalDRC(type message location1 location2 …)
axlDBCreateVia(padstack location net …)
axlShapeCreate / axlDBCreatePath …
tools.example:
when( addDrcs
  axlDBCreateExternalDRC("SMALL_SEG" "segment shorter than aspect ratio" seg->startEnd))
tools.notes: Database writes should be wrapped in a transaction (`axlDBTransactionStart`/`End`) so a failed script can be undone cleanly.

tools.name: SKILL: registering a custom command
tools.description: `axlCmdRegister` publishes a SKILL procedure as a first-class PCB Editor command, so it can be typed in the command window, bound with `alias`/`funckey`, put on a menu or toolbar, and can participate in the normal interactive command loop. Loading the SKILL file from an `allegro.ilinit` in the user's pcbenv/skill directory makes the command available every session.
tools.usage: axlCmdRegister( "mycmd" 'myProcedure ?cmdType "interactive")
tools.example:
;; in %HOME%/pcbenv/skill/mytools.il
procedure( myCrossCmd() … )
axlCmdRegister("crosscmd" 'myCrossCmd ?cmdType "interactive")
;; in allegro.ilinit:  load("mytools.il")
tools.notes: Register names must be unique; colliding with a built-in command silently shadows it.

tools.name: extracta
tools.description: The standalone Cadence utility that extracts data from a binary .brd or .dra and writes it as delimited ASCII. A command file lists the database classes and fields wanted (components, pins, nets, vias, shapes, stackup) and extracta produces a text table, which makes it the supported way for scripts and third-party tools to read an Allegro board without the GUI. It is also the step Altium's Allegro importer relies on.
tools.usage:
extracta.exe <board.brd> <command_file> <output_file>
extracta -version

parameters.name: board file
parameters.description: Binary .brd or .dra to read; extracta must be at least as new as the file's version.

parameters.name: command file
parameters.description: Text file naming the views/classes and fields to extract and the delimiter.

parameters.name: output file
parameters.description: Delimited ASCII result.

tools.example:
extracta.exe mainboard.brd comps.cmd comps.txt
# comps.cmd requests COMPONENT: REFDES CLASS SYM_NAME SYM_X SYM_Y SYM_ROTATE SYM_MIRROR
tools.notes: Check compatibility first with `extracta -version`: it refuses boards saved by a newer release than itself. In a standard install extracta.exe is already on the system PATH.

tools.name: dbdoctor
tools.description: The database repair and upgrade utility. It regenerates the connectivity and shape data of a board, fixes database inconsistencies, and brings an old .brd forward to the installed release's format — which is exactly what is needed when a legacy board refuses to open or reports corruption. A GUI front end (dbdoctor_ui) and a command-line form both ship in the installation's tools/bin directory.
tools.usage: dbdoctor <input.brd> [options]; or run dbdoctor_ui.exe from <install>\tools\bin and pick input/output files

parameters.name: Regenerate xnets / connectivity
parameters.description: Rebuilds the derived connectivity data.

parameters.name: Check/repair database
parameters.description: Finds and corrects structural inconsistencies.

parameters.name: Output file
parameters.description: Repaired board written to a new file, leaving the original intact.

tools.example: Run dbdoctor_ui.exe, input old_16_6.brd, output old_repaired.brd, tick the regenerate options, Run — then open the repaired board in the current release.
tools.notes: Always write to a new output file; do not repair in place over the only copy of a board.

tools.name: a2dxf / DXF import and export
tools.description: Exchanges board geometry with mechanical CAD in DXF. Inside the editor, File > Export > DXF writes selected layers/subclasses as DXF entities and File > Import > DXF brings mechanical outlines, keep-outs and connector positions in onto chosen subclasses. `a2dxf` is the batch-mode Cadence translator that performs the Allegro-to-DXF conversion without the GUI.
tools.usage: File > Export > DXF… / File > Import > DXF…; batch: a2dxf <board> <options>
tools.example: File > Import > DXF > file enclosure.dxf > units mm > map DXF layer OUTLINE to class BOARD GEOMETRY subclass OUTLINE > Import.
tools.notes: Set the DXF units and scale explicitly on import; a wrong unit assumption silently produces a board outline 25.4 times too big or small.

tools.name: netrev / net_in (logic import utilities)
tools.description: The command-line counterparts of File > Import > Logic. `netrev` processes a Cadence third-party or pst*.dat logic package into the board, reporting differences and unresolved footprints into netrev.lst; `net_in` handles the netlist input path for the older flow. They allow the schematic-to-board update to run inside a scripted build rather than through the GUI dialog.
tools.usage: netrev / net_in invoked from the Cadence shell with the netlist directory and target board
tools.example:
1. In Capture: Tools > Create Netlist > PCB Editor tab to write pstchip.dat/pstxnet.dat/pstxprt.dat.
2. Run the logic import (GUI File > Import > Logic, or the netrev utility) against the board.
3. Read netrev.lst for unresolved symbols before continuing.
tools.notes: Exact switches vary by release and are not published outside the installed documentation — check `<install>/doc` for your version rather than assuming a flag.

tools.name: OrCAD X Presto
tools.description: The rebuilt PCB editor introduced with OrCAD X: a modern canvas with a properties-driven UI, integrated constraint editing, real-time DRC, dynamic shapes, interactive routing with push and shove, an integrated 3D view and direct manufacturing output — all on the same .brd database as classic PCB Editor, so designs move between the two. It targets the workflow of a single designer who wants Allegro's constraint engine without its command-line-era interface.
tools.usage: Launched as OrCAD X Presto; opens the same .brd files as OrCAD PCB Editor
tools.example: Open the .brd in Presto, use the Design Setup panel for stackup and constraints, route with the interactive router, then generate outputs from the Manufacturing panel.
tools.notes: SKILL and .scr automation are features of the classic PCB Editor; Presto's own automation surface is more limited, so keep scripted steps in the classic editor.
